features.name: Business Central AI Resources
features.description: Microsoft managed Azure OpenAI resources that allow publishers to use large language models without independently procuring and managing Azure OpenAI subscriptions for customers. Consumption-based approach where customers are billed directly by Microsoft. Available in SaaS production environments only. Supports GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini models.
features.status_evidence_quote: we're moving BC or Business Central AI resources from private preview, that means by invitation only, uh to a public preview
caveats: Partners still need to use their own subscription when prototyping, developing, testing and troubleshooting in non-production and non-SaaS environments
Consumption-based direct billing is being added in this release
Available in SaaS and production environments only
No embeddings support at time of recording
Billing details not finalized at recording time

features.name: Consumption-based billing for AI resource use
features.description: Direct billing of customers for AI resource consumption across ISV solutions through the Business Central AI resources. Microsoft charges customers directly based on consumption. Customers can track usage, set limits, and receive a single invoice across all ISVs using Business Central AI Resources.
features.status_evidence_quote: So this will be a consumptionbased uh approach where the customers will build directly from Microsoft.
caveats: Implementation details and rollout timeline not specified in first segment

features.name: Content safety with blocking policy
features.description: Built-in content safety measures including blocking policy for calls to Azure OpenAI, with filters for hate, violence, sexual content, self-harm, jailbreak detection, and cross-prompt injection attack protection. Implemented as part of responsible AI measures along with system prompt additions.
caveats: Better protection against prompt injection attacks is in the plans but not yet implemented
These policies may slightly change model behavior between on-premise and production environments

features.name: Set managed resource authorization function
features.description: AL code function that allows developers to use Business Central AI resources by specifying Azure OpenAI account name, API key, and deployment name.
caveats: Partners must still have an approved Azure OpenAI subscription for compliance verification, though resources are not consumed
Requires specifying a deployment name from available models

features.name: Bring your own Azure OpenAI subscription
features.description: Alternative approach allowing developers to use their own Azure OpenAI subscription instead of managed BC AI resources, primarily for development, testing, troubleshooting and special use cases.
caveats: Recommended only for development or special needs, not for production deployment
Use set authorization function instead of set managed resource authorization
Data source capabilities not supported when bringing your own Azure OpenAI subscription

features.name: Conditional code pattern for development and production
features.description: Code pattern that uses environment information to determine whether to use bring-your-own Azure OpenAI subscription during development or managed BC AI resources in production.
caveats: Testing should be done in on-premise environment before deploying to SaaS production due to potentially different model behavior

features.name: Data residency control for AI calls
features.description: Administrators can control whether AI calls cross geographical boundaries through the copilot and agent capabilities page in Business Central.
caveats: Only applicable when Azure OpenAI deployment is available in the same geography

features.name: System prompts for AI safety
features.description: Meta prompts appended to developer prompts as part of content safety measures when using the Business Central AI resources toolkit.
caveats: May cause slight behavior differences between on-premise testing with own subscription and production deployment
Developers should test thoroughly in sandbox before customer deployment

features.name: Model deprecation notifications via telemetry
features.description: Developer telemetry signals notify developers when Azure OpenAI models are being deprecated, allowing time to migrate to new models.
caveats: Model deprecation deadlines are stricter than AL deprecation deadlines
Failure to migrate before deprecation may result in automatic model change, potentially affecting feature behavior

features.name: Azure OpenAI Deployments code unit
features.description: Code unit that contains available Azure OpenAI model deployments that developers can use when configuring managed resource authorization.

features.name: Data source capabilities in AI Resources
features.description: Data source capabilities from Azure OpenAI are currently not supported in Business Central AI Resources toolkit, nor when bringing your own Azure OpenAI subscription.
caveats: Not available
No retrieval augmented generation support

features.name: Non-OpenAI models support
features.description: Non-OpenAI models such as DeepSeek are not currently supported in the Business Central AI Resources toolkit because Microsoft only exposes capabilities it uses internally.
caveats: Third-party models not supported

features.name: AI Resources model availability
features.description: Production-ready models available are GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini. More models will likely be added in the future. Users will be notified through telemetry when new models arrive or old ones are deprecated.
caveats: Limited to two models at recording time
Future model additions not specified

features.name: Embeddings support
features.description: Embeddings are not supported at the time of recording in Business Central AI Resources, but semantic search capabilities similar to embeddings are planned for approximately half a year to a year in the future.
features.status_evidence_quote: we do not support uh embeddings although we have plans in probably next release uh in a you know half a year to a
caveats: Not available now
Timeline is approximate
